title: Customer-tailored IaC extension patterns for private VPC deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers deploying Redwood Private require per-tenant network and compliance customizations (route tables, NAT/firewall rules, private PKI endpoints, onboarded logging sinks) while still receiving automated runtime upgrades and standardized healthchecks. Current repo patterns (flat module overrides and ad-hoc var files) lead to drift, risky manual edits during upgrades, and difficulty running CI-driven health validations.

Goal: Define a repeatable set of IaC extension patterns that let customers express lightweight customizations without forking core modules. Patterns must support safe upgrades (schema changes), pre/post upgrade health gates, and explicit optics for customer-impacting edits. Implement docs, example blueprints, and CI hooks to validate upgrade compatibility for each tenant before rollout.

Scope: module composition and extension surface (customer-layer), variable scoping conventions, safe upgrade hooks, health-check integration, CI validation workflows, and migration path for 10 existing Private customers. Not in scope: full rewrite of core modules or changing runtime APIs.

Non-goals: Provide a generic “one-size-fits-all” adapter that covers every networking edge-case; instead we provide composable patterns and example shims for common variants.
acceptance_criteria: Provide three documented extension patterns: (1) tenant-override shim, (2) parameterized feature flags, (3) composition via light-weight wrapper modules
Create example blueprints for at least NAT-restricted tenant, split-log-sink tenant, and customer-managed DNS tenant
Implement pre-upgrade CI job that runs a compatibility validator and health-check simulator against a tenant staging workspace
Add upgrade hooks: terraform plan diffs, drift-safe migration steps, and an automated preflight that can block upgrades on high-risk changes
Healthchecks wired to Terraform outputs and a minimal external probe (lambda) with documented failure modes and remediation steps
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Design and docs (2w) - define variable namespacing, module interface contracts, and shim patterns; produce blueprints. Phase 2: Core refs & validators (2w) - implement a compatibility validator that inspects tfvars, provider versions, and module inputs; add a preflight pipeline template. Phase 3: Examples & migrations (2w) - convert 3 pilot customers to the new pattern, capture migration scripts and rollback steps. Phase 4: Integrations (1w) - wire health-check probes and add dashboard signals to Console for tenant-level upgrade status.
testing_plan: Unit: linter and tf module tests for schema compatibility. Integration: spin up ephemeral tenant workspaces in CI using terraform workspace namespacing against a VPC mock (localstack + kind) to run plan/apply-destroy. Upgrade test: simulated module version bump pipeline that validates pre/post healthchecks and compares resource diffs. Canary: rollout to pilot customers behind a canary toggle with automatic rollback on health regression.
rollout_plan: 1) Run internal validation on staging tenants; 2) Work with two pilot customers to migrate to tenant-shim pattern; 3) Once stable, offer as upgrade path for remaining customers with documented runbook; 4) During platform release (private-2025.03) enable opt-in auto-validation for Dedicated and Private tenants.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: customers with heavy customizations may still require forks. Mitigation: provide well-documented 'escape hatch' with guarded module subdirectories and strong upgrade recommendation docs. Risk: Terraform schema changes break customer overlays. Mitigation: compatibility validator + preflight that blocks risky changes and surfaces human-readable migration steps. Risk: healthchecks create noisy alerts. Mitigation: multi-stage health gates with suppression windows and clear remediation playbooks.
